content.user_title: Classify Businesses Against a Single Sector
content.value_statement: Business descriptions can make industry matching and website template selection inconsistent. This guide outlines keyword-based sector matching and site archetype choices for an AI assistant.
actual_capabilities: Describes keyword-based matching of a business description against one configured sector.
Provides a bakery example with identified keywords, a match result, and an illustrative score.
Outlines sector-based choices for website sections, tone, imagery, and calls to action.
Recommends a generic site archetype when classification confidence is low.
Describes generating a standalone Python classifier, but does not include the implementation.
limitations: Only SKILL.md is included; executable scripts, extension source, and templates are absent.
The free approach addresses one configured sector at a time, not comprehensive multi-sector classification.
The guide targets Belgian and Benelux SMEs; unusual or multi-activity businesses may require a generic result.
No keyword dictionary, scoring formula, confidence calibration, or concrete JSON schema is supplied.

use_cases.title: Review Lead Sector Matches
use_cases.description: Compare supplied prospect descriptions with one selected sector before assigning industry labels in a CRM.

use_cases.title: Plan Sector-Based Demo Sites
use_cases.description: Use business evidence to propose website sections, tone, imagery, and calls to action, with a generic fallback for uncertain cases.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Lightweight Classifier
use_cases.description: Ask an assistant to draft a single-sector Python classifier, then inspect and test the generated implementation before integration.

prompt_templates.title: Match One Business
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify this description against Food and Beverage: Artisanal bakery in Ghent specializing in sourdough bread and local pastries. Identify supporting keywords.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect the documented bakery example.

prompt_templates.title: Assess an Uncertain Match
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [business description] against [sector] using [keywords]. Explain missing evidence and recommend a generic archetype when confidence is low.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: handle incomplete or ambiguous business information.

prompt_templates.title: Propose a Site Archetype
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [business description] and [public listing text], assess [sector]. Propose sections, tone, imagery, and a call to action. Separate evidence from assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a sector-informed demo website.

prompt_templates.title: Draft and Test a Classifier
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft classifier_lite.py for [sector] using [keywords]. Define scoring explicitly. Include positive, negative, and ambiguous tests. Do not claim the guide supplies executable code.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: create and validate an implementation from the guide.

output_examples.input: Match an artisanal Ghent bakery specializing in sourdough bread and local pastries against Food and Beverage.
output: The guide illustrates an 85/100 score, but does not supply the scoring formula.

output_examples.input: Assess a business described only as a local provider of several unrelated services, then choose a site archetype.
output: Sector: insufficient evidence for a specific match.
Additional evidence needed: primary service descriptions and public listing details.

best_practices: Supply the target sector, explicit keywords, and relevant business text before requesting a classification.
Use a generic archetype when evidence is sparse or the business spans several activities.
Review generated scripts and test representative matches, nonmatches, and ambiguous cases before pipeline integration.
anti_patterns: Treating the public guide as an installed classifier with bundled executable assets.
Interpreting an illustrative keyword score as a calibrated probability or independently verified business classification.
Assuming the free single-sector approach includes the paid version's 12 archetypes or AI-driven analysis.

faq.question: What is included in this package?
faq.answer: The package includes one public SKILL.md guide. Scripts, extension source, and templates from the original package are not included.

faq.question: How does the free classification approach work?
faq.answer: The guide describes keyword-based matching against one configured sector. It does not provide the keyword set or scoring implementation.

faq.question: Does this package include a Python classifier?
faq.answer: No. The guide describes generating classifier_lite.py, but that file is not included. Any generated implementation requires review and testing.

faq.question: Does it retrieve websites or public listings automatically?
faq.answer: The guide describes those sources, but includes no retrieval implementation. You must supply source text or arrange appropriate tools separately.

faq.question: What happens when a business does not fit clearly?
faq.answer: The guide recommends a generic archetype when confidence is low. Unusual or multi-activity businesses may need manual review.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this guide?
faq.answer: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can use the instructions. Executable classification still requires an implementation beyond this package.
